Entry Shipyards of the Iron Islands Longships didn't come naturally; they required lumber, nails, tar, skilled carpenters, and constant patching. The lords regarded the dockyard as the foundation of sea power, and shipbuilders understood that a ship could provide a family with income for several years; more ships meant strength, and also meant more Any break in the place of origin, checkpoints, shipping schedules, debts and protection fees will immediately make the nobles in the distance feel the changes in price and power.

Entry Shipyards of the Iron Islands Longships didn't come naturally; they required lumber, nails, tar, skilled carpenters, and constant patching. The lords regarded the dockyard as the foundation of sea power, and shipbuilders understood that a ship could provide a family with income for several years; more ships meant strength, and also meant more Some people turn raw materials into tools, cloth and medicine, others set festivals and taboos for exchange; wealth is piled up by many hands, and rarely belongs to just one name.
